_about: Grammar points for the walk along the old Tōkaidō, one post town per stop, in the usual beginner order, grouped into chapters. Explanations are written for Oishii and cross-checked against Tae Kim's Guide to Learning Japanese (guidetojapanese.org); 'check' names the section each was compared with. Japanese in these cards marks kanji as {kanji|reading}, so the game shows kanji the player has stamped and kana for the rest. Example sentences are never written here: tools/grammar_build.py picks native Tatoeba sentences for each point. 'wrong' lists particles that are clearly wrong for this use, for the particle drills; 'also' lists other particles that are also right. Every 'wrong' particle must be wrong in any sentence for that point (を can mark a path with movement verbs, can stand where も replaced it, and で marks where events happen), so points where that can't be promised get no particle drill.

stops.note: The bridge in Edo where the Tōkaidō starts. Japan's national road distances from Tokyo are still measured from a marker on it.
The first post town, by the sea at the edge of Edo.
The second post town, where travellers crossed the Tama River by ferry.
The third post town, along a hillside above the bay, lined with tea houses.
The fourth post town. Past it the road climbs Gontazaka, the first steep hill out of Edo.
The fifth post town, often the first night's stop for travellers walking out of Edo.
The sixth post town, a temple town around Yugyō-ji, near the road to Enoshima.
The seventh post town, on the flat plain of the Sagami River.
The eighth post town, by a long beach on Sagami Bay.
The ninth post town, a castle town at the foot of the Hakone hills.
The tenth post town, high in the hills, with the famous checkpoint where travellers were stopped and searched.
The 11th post town, at the foot of the Hakone pass, known for Mishima Taisha shrine and spring water from Mount Fuji.
The 12th post town, on Suruga Bay.
The 13th post town, with one of the road's finest views of Mount Fuji.
The 14th post town, where the road bends and Mount Fuji appears on the left: the famous "left-hand Fuji".
The 15th post town, painted by Hiroshige under a night of snow.
The 16th post town, before the Satta Pass and its views of Fuji over the sea. Today it is known for sakura shrimp.
The 17th post town, a seaside town by Seiken-ji temple.
The 18th post town, near the port of Shimizu and the pine beach of Miho.
The 19th post town, the castle town of Sunpu, where Tokugawa Ieyasu retired. Today it is Shizuoka city.
The 20th post town, famous for tororo-jiru, a soup of grated mountain yam.

notes: は marks the topic: what the sentence is about. As a particle it is said "wa", not "ha".
です ends the sentence politely, a bit like "is" or "am".
wa_desu.check: Tae Kim: Particles (は topic); Expressing state-of-being (です)

ja_nai.pattern: A は B じゃないです
ja_nai.make: noun + じゃないです (or ではありません, more formal)
notes: じゃないです and じゃありません both mean "is not". ではありません is the more formal, written form.
Put か at the end of a polite sentence to make it a question. The word order doesn't change.
の joins two nouns: the first one describes the second. {私|わたし}の{本|ほん} is "my book", {日本|にほん}の{車|くるま} is "a Japanese car".

kore.pattern: これ・それ・あれ・どれ
kore.en: this one, that one, that one over there, which one
kore.make: used on their own, like a noun
notes: これ is near me, それ is near you, あれ is over there, away from us both. どれ asks "which one?".
kore.check: Tae Kim: Nouns (demonstratives こそあど)

kono.pattern: この・その・あの・どの + noun
kono.en: this…, that…, that… over there, which…
notes: The same idea as これ・それ・あれ・どれ, but always followed by a noun: この{本|ほん} "this book".
kono.check: Tae Kim: Nouns (demonstratives こそあど)

wo_obj.en: A is what the action is done to
notes: を marks the object: the thing being eaten, read or bought. It is said "o".

masu.make: verb stem + ます: {食|た}べる → {食|た}べます, {行|い}く → {行|い}きます
notes: ます is the polite form of a verb. It covers what you do now, usually, or will do.
For る-verbs drop る ({食|た}べる → {食|た}べ). For う-verbs change the last sound to the い row ({行|い}く → {行|い}き). する → します, {来|く}る → {来|き}ます.
masu.check: Tae Kim: Polite form and verb stems

masen.make: verb stem + ません: {食|た}べません, {行|い}きません
notes: Swap ます for ません to say you don't or won't do something.
masen.check: Tae Kim: Polite form and verb stems

ni_dest.pattern: place に / へ {行|い}きます
ni_dest.make: place + に or へ + {行|い}きます / {来|き}ます / {帰|かえ}ります
notes: に or へ marks where you are going. With {行|い}く, {来|く}る and {帰|かえ}る both are fine; へ (said "e") stresses the direction.

mo_also.make: noun + も (in place of は, が or を)
notes: も means "also". It replaces は, が or を: {私|わたし}も{行|い}きます "I'm going too".
で marks where something is done: {図書館|としょかん}で{勉強|べんきょう}します "I study at the library".
For where something simply is, use に instead (Fujisawa).

de_means.make: tool, vehicle or language + で + verb
notes: The same で also marks how you do something: バスで{行|い}きます "go by bus", {日本語|にほんご}で{話|はな}します "speak in Japanese".

to_with.make: person + と + verb, often と{一緒|いっしょ}に
notes: と after a person means doing something together with them. {一緒|いっしょ}に ("together") is often added.

mashita.make: verb stem + ました: {食|た}べました, {行|い}きました
notes: Swap ます for ました to talk about the past.

masendeshita.make: verb stem + ませんでした
notes: Add でした to ません for "didn't": {行|い}きませんでした "I didn't go".

aru_iru.pattern: A が あります / います
aru_iru.make: thing + が + あります; person or animal + が + います
notes: あります is for things and plants, います for people and animals.
が marks the thing that is there.
aru_iru.check: Tae Kim: Particles (が); the verbs ある and いる

ni_exist.pattern: place に A が あります / います
ni_exist.make: place + に + あります / います
notes: に marks where something is. Compare で, which marks where something is done (Hodogaya).

i_adj.make: {高|たか}いです; not: {高|たか}くないです; before a noun: {高|たか}い{山|やま}
notes: い-adjectives end in い. Add です to be polite.
For "not", change the last い to くない: {高|たか}い → {高|たか}くないです. いい is irregular: よくないです.

na_adj.make: {静|しず}かです; not: {静|しず}かじゃないです; before a noun: {静|しず}かな{町|まち}
notes: な-adjectives work like nouns: {静|しず}かです, {静|しず}かじゃないです.
Before a noun they take な: {静|しず}かな{町|まち} "a quiet town".
Asking "won't you…?" is a soft, polite way to invite someone: {一緒|いっしょ}に{行|い}きませんか "Would you like to go together?".
ましょう suggests doing something together: {行|い}きましょう "Let's go". ましょうか means "shall I…?" or "shall we…?".

ga_suki.en: like A (also dislike, good at, bad at)
ga_suki.make: thing + が + {好|す}き / {嫌|きら}い / {上手|じょうず} / {下手|へた} + です
notes: {好|す}き (like), {嫌|きら}い (dislike), {上手|じょうず} (good at) and {下手|へた} (bad at) take が for the thing: {猫|ねこ}が{好|す}きです "I like cats".
ga_suki.check: Tae Kim: Particles (が); な-adjectives (好き, 嫌い)

notes: ね at the end looks for agreement: "isn't it?". よ tells the listener something new: "you know".
ne_yo.check: Tae Kim: Sentence-ending particles (ね, よ)

te_kudasai.make: て-form + ください: {待|ま}ってください
notes: The て-form joins a verb to what comes next. る-verbs: {食|た}べる → {食|た}べて. う-verbs change sound: {書|か}く → {書|か}いて, {泳|およ}ぐ → {泳|およ}いで, {話|はな}す → {話|はな}して, {待|ま}つ・{取|と}る・{買|か}う → {待|ま}って・{取|と}って・{買|か}って, {飲|の}む・{遊|あそ}ぶ・{死|し}ぬ → {飲|の}んで・{遊|あそ}んで・{死|し}んで. {行|い}く → {行|い}って, する → して, {来|く}る → {来|き}て.
て-form + ください asks someone politely to do something.
te_kudasai.check: Tae Kim: Te-form; requests (ください)

te_mo_ii.pattern: verb て も いいですか
notes: て-form + もいいです means "it's all right to…". Add か to ask for permission: {写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}ってもいいですか "May I take a photo?".
te_mo_ii.check: Tae Kim: Expressing permission (てもいい)

te_wa_ikenai.pattern: verb て は いけません
notes: て-form + はいけません means "you must not": ここで{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}ってはいけません "You mustn't take photos here". Just what the guards at the Hakone checkpoint would say.
te_wa_ikenai.check: Tae Kim: Expressing prohibition (てはいけない)

tai.make: verb stem + たい: {食|た}べたい, {行|い}きたい
notes: Swap ます for たい to say what you want to do: {日本|にほん}に{行|い}きたいです "I want to go to Japan".
たい works like an い-adjective: {行|い}きたくないです "I don't want to go".

hoshii.pattern: A が ほしいです
hoshii.make: thing + が + ほしいです
notes: ほしい is an い-adjective for wanting things: {新|あたら}しい{車|くるま}がほしいです "I want a new car". For wanting to do something, use たい.

te_iru.en: is doing; is in a state
te_iru.make: て-form + います: {食|た}べています
notes: て-form + いる says something is going on now: {今|いま}{食|た}べています "I'm eating now".
It also describes a state that lasts: {東京|とうきょう}に{住|す}んでいます "I live in Tokyo", {知|し}っています "I know". In casual speech the い is often dropped: {食|た}べてる.

ni_time.make: time + に: {七時|しちじ}に, {日曜日|にちようび}に
notes: に marks a set time: {七時|しちじ}に{起|お}きます "I get up at seven".
Words like {今日|きょう}, {明日|あした}, {毎日|まいにち} and {今|いま} don't take に.

kara_made.pattern: A から B まで
kara_made.make: time or place + から; time or place + まで
notes: から marks a starting point and まで an end point, in time or space: {九時|くじ}から{五時|ごじ}まで "from nine to five", {駅|えき}まで "as far as the station".
kara_made.check: Tae Kim: Particles (から, まで)

plain_dict.make: the dictionary form: {行|い}く, {食|た}べる, する
notes: With friends and family, Japanese drops です and ます. The plain form of a verb is the one in the dictionary: {明日|あした}{行|い}く "I'll go tomorrow".
It means the same as the ます form, just casual.

da.make: {学生|がくせい}だ, {静|しず}かだ; not: {学生|がくせい}じゃない
notes: だ is the casual です after nouns and な-adjectives. Its negative is じゃない. い-adjectives never take だ: {高|たか}い on its own is already a full sentence.

plain_nai.make: る-verbs: {食|た}べない; う-verbs, last sound to the あ row: {行|い}かない, {買|か}わない; しない, {来|こ}ない
notes: The ない form is the casual ません. For う-verbs ending in う, it becomes わ: {買|か}う → {買|か}わない. ある becomes just ない.

plain_ta.make: the て-form with た: {食|た}べた, {行|い}った, {飲|の}んだ; ない → なかった
notes: The た form is the casual ました. It is made just like the て-form, with た for て and だ for で.
For the past negative, ない becomes なかった: {行|い}かなかった "I didn't go".

deshita.pattern: noun でした / だった
deshita.make: {学生|がくせい}でした (polite), {学生|がくせい}だった (casual)
notes: でした is the past of です after nouns and な-adjectives: {昨日|きのう}は{雨|あめ}でした "It was rainy yesterday". だった is the casual past.

i_adj_past.make: {高|たか}い → {高|たか}かった(です); not: {高|たか}くなかった(です)
notes: い-adjectives change for the past themselves: the last い becomes かった. {楽|たの}しかったです "It was fun". いい → よかった.
から after a sentence gives a reason: {暑|あつ}いから、{窓|まど}を{開|あ}けます "It's hot, so I'll open the window". It follows a plain or a polite form.
が between two sentences means "but": {高|たか}いですが、おいしいです "It's expensive, but it's tasty". It is often softer than English "but".
ga_but.check: Tae Kim: Compound sentences (が, けど)

naide_kudasai.pattern: verb ないで ください
naide_kudasai.make: ない form + でください: {行|い}かないでください
notes: The ない form + でください asks someone not to do something: {忘|わす}れないでください "Please don't forget".
naide_kudasai.check: Tae Kim: Requests (ないでください)

nakereba.pattern: verb なければ なりません
nakereba.make: ない form, ない → なければなりません: {行|い}かなければなりません
notes: It literally says "if I don't go, it won't do": {帰|かえ}らなければなりません "I have to go home". なくてはいけません means the same.
nakereba.check: Tae Kim: Must (なければならない)

tekara.make: て-form + から: {食|た}べてから
notes: て-form + から means "after doing": {宿題|しゅくだい}をしてから{遊|あそ}びます "I'll play after doing my homework". Compare から after a plain sentence, "because" (Okitsu).

mae_ni.make: dictionary form + {前|まえ}に; noun + の{前|まえ}に
notes: {前|まえ}に means "before": {寝|ね}る{前|まえ}に "before going to bed", {食事|しょくじ}の{前|まえ}に "before the meal". The verb stays in the dictionary form, even when the sentence is in the past.

hou_ga.pattern: A より B の ほうが…
hou_ga.make: A + より, B + のほうが + adjective
notes: より means "than" and のほうが marks the winner: {電車|でんしゃ}のほうが{速|はや}いです "The train is faster", バスより{電車|でんしゃ}のほうが{速|はや}いです "The train is faster than the bus".
hou_ga.check: Tae Kim: Comparison (より, ほう)

notes: {一番|いちばん} means "number one", so before an adjective it means "the most": {一番|いちばん}{好|す}きです "I like it best".
が marks the one doing something or being described: {雪|ゆき}が{降|ふ}っています "Snow is falling", {目|め}が{痛|いた}いです "My eyes hurt".
は says what you're talking about; が points at who or what. Questions use が: {誰|だれ}が{来|き}ますか "Who's coming?".
ga_subj.check: Tae Kim: Particles (が, and は compared)

chapters.name: Nihonbashi to Hakone
chapters.note: Polite sentences: です, ます and the particles.

chapters.name: Mishima to Mariko
chapters.note: Wants, ongoing actions, time, and the plain forms friends use with each other.
